fixed_work.cache: flush before every batch; distinct request prefixes

natural.cache: cold for all; additionally prime session prefix before session-hit

reporting: Report each fixed-work cell separately, aggregate output tokens / client batch makespan, TTFT and decode throughput. Forced output after EOS is an engine throughput diagnostic, not a quality claim. Natural requests retain local-v1 stopping, sampling, budgets and quality rubric. Preserve every sample and error; no p95/p99, universal lead or quality-equivalence claim from this small benchmark. Measure both SGLang DFlash2 prefill sizes; report both or explicitly label a per-cell best-of-two baseline. Do not silently select the weaker configuration.
memory_accounting: Exclusive GPU windows. Apply the same 64 GiB host MemAvailable-drop budget relative to each pre-launch baseline, a 16 GiB absolute floor, and a 64 GiB cgroup cap. The host delta includes other processes and cache reclamation; the cgroup alone does not contain CUDA unified allocations. Report observed minimum MemAvailable and engine allocations separately; do not add overlapping RSS and CUDA counts. Abort rather than claim equal memory if a profile exceeds the budget.
state_capacity_note: Internal recurrent slots are not comparable across engines. SGLang requires several per active request; 24 allows four active requests. Sharar uses 12. Both remain subject to the same total memory budget. This clarification followed the excluded capacity smoke; the completed Sharar plain run used the identical inputs, sampling and its unchanged 12-slot configuration.
